result.title: Decoupled Predictive Decision Making: A Shared Conditional Predictor for Agents
result.summary: Agent decisions depend on empirical relationships that deployment observations reveal and task descriptions alone may leave unresolved. We introduce Decoupled Predictive Decision Making (DPDM), an architecture that formulates heterogeneous agent decisions as conditional prediction with a shared pretrained learner. Language models provide semantic representations of current and historical records, while a general-purpose conditional predictor predicts task-defined targets from the represented evidence. Pretraining supplies reusable inference capability; deployment evidence instantiates problem-specific predictions without updating either model's neural parameters. Tool judgments, candidate preferences, and reasoning assessments share an evidence-and-query interface, with predictions mapped to choices by a decision rule. This architecture establishes complementary sources of agent capability: semantic knowledge acquired through language pretraining and empirical inference acquired through structured-data pretraining. A single frozen LimiX-2 predictor serves all five task categories. With Qwen3.5-27B as the semantic encoder, DPDM raises mean accuracy across 50 benchmarks from 78.80% with few-shot prompting to 84.92% under their respective evaluated history budgets, and reaches 82.33% with identical histories and queries. On ToolPRMBench's BFCL and ToolSandbox tasks, absolute accuracy gains are 34.26% and 28.87%, respectively, at the methods' respective evaluated history budgets. Accuracy improves as history grows. With identical imbalanced histories, mean balanced accuracy improves by an absolute 14.51% across five reasoning-step assessment tasks and four encoders. DPDM makes learning from experience an independently improvable foundation-model capability, creating a shared route for advances in conditional prediction to improve decisions across agent tasks.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 DPDM 架构：以语言模型编码当前与历史记录作为语义表示，再由冻结的通用条件预测器根据这些证据预测任务目标，在不更新神经参数的情况下把预测映射为决策，并在 50 个基准上评估。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「语义编码器＋冻结条件预测器＋证据驱动推断」的解耦，可能为 LVR 中视觉证据与参数知识的分工、以及在 latent 表示上做预测式读取和贡献分配提供可核查线索；但该工作为文本/结构化数据 agent 任务，无视觉推理状态实验。
